model_output.verdict: A mathematics teacher with concrete data projects is making a transition into analytics.
write_up: Your resume shows a Mathematics Teacher moving toward data analytics, with classroom assessment work and two data projects behind that move. I read it first for Mathematics Teacher because that's your most recent named role. For analytics jobs, a recruiter will need to connect the teaching work to the tools and decisions in your projects.

The Excel dashboard is your best model: it names what you built, what it tracked, and the period it covered. The next line also says the math department used it to decide which units needed re-teaching. Your data projects sit below your teaching experience, though they're central to the transition you want to make.

Let's bring the projects closer to the top and replace the broad summary with your actual data work. Then add a few details about how you used assessment results and what you found in the housing analysis.

cards.line: Passionate about using data to tell stories and drive decisions.
cards.cannot_tell: This doesn't tell a recruiter which data work you've done or what analytics job you want. Your dashboard and bootcamp project can make the transition concrete.
cards.example: Mathematics Teacher transitioning into [target role], with experience analyzing student assessment data and building an Excel dashboard tracking AP Statistics pass rates and quiz scores
cards.question: Which analytics job are you targeting?

cards.line: Data Projects sits below Professional Experience.
cards.cannot_tell: Your projects show Python, SQL, Tableau, and Excel work that matters for the transition. A recruiter looking for analytics experience has to get through both teaching roles before reaching them.
cards.question: Would you move Data Projects above Professional Experience for analytics applications?

cards.line: - Developed and implemented engaging curriculum aligned with state standards

cards.question: What curriculum unit or teaching material did you develop and implement?

cards.line: - Analyzed student assessment data to identify learning gaps and adjust instruction
cards.cannot_tell: The connection between analysis and instruction is useful for your transition, but the adjustment is still a blank. What did you change after finding a learning gap?
cards.example: Analyzed student assessment data to identify learning gaps and adjusted instruction by [instructional change]
cards.question: What instructional change did you make after analyzing assessment data?

cards.line: - Served as Math Department Data Lead, compiling benchmark results for department meetings
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see that you compiled benchmark results, but not what you put together for the meetings. A named report or other deliverable would show more of the data work.
cards.example: Served as Math Department Data Lead, compiling benchmark results into [deliverable] for department meetings
cards.question: What did you prepare from the benchmark results for department meetings?

cards.line: - Participated in professional learning communities
cards.cannot_tell: Participation alone doesn't show what you contributed. If there was a useful piece of work from these meetings, name it; otherwise, this line can make room for your projects.
cards.example: Participated in professional learning communities and contributed [work or deliverable]
cards.question: What work did you contribute through the professional learning communities?

cards.line: - Presented findings to a panel of instructors and peers
cards.cannot_tell: The audience is clear, but the findings aren't. Naming one finding would show what came out of the housing analysis.
cards.example: Presented findings on [finding] to a panel of instructors and peers
cards.question: What finding did you present about Austin housing affordability?

cards.line: - Built an Excel dashboard tracking AP Statistics pass rates and quiz scores over three years
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It puts your own action, the tool, and the measures together, so nobody has to guess what the dashboard contained.
